note: A mode is taught by its one colour note: hear it change, find it in two positions with the root and the 6th lit, then use it where it is also a chord tone. No block repeats a position or a task.

exercise.title: D Dorian: find the 6th
exercise.focus: D Dorian · root on the A and low E strings · Dm7-G7
exercise.why: Dorian is natural minor with a raised 6th; hearing and aiming at that one note is what makes it sound Dorian.

sections.text: Dorian differs from natural minor by one note, so practise that note, not seven.
Press Play: the first half is D natural minor, the second half D Dorian, over a held Dm. Play along in the neck view and listen for the bar where one note brightens.
The note that changed is {{6}}: B, not B♭. Play the box with {{1}} at the 5th fret of the A string up and down, then play {{6}} and resolve it to {{1}} three times.
Same mode, the box with {{1}} on the 10th fret of the low E. Find every {{6}} in it before you play the box, then play it up and down at 80.
B is also the 3rd of G7, so Dorian fits Dm7-G7 perfectly. Improvise in either box; land on {{d}} over Dm7 and on {{b}} over G7.
